seo.title: The North Face: conversational shopping assistant (IBM Watson XPS) - 60% click-through to recos (pilot)
seo.meta_description: In 2015-2016, The North Face launched XPS, a conversational shopping assistant on IBM Watson that recommended jackets by use case. Pilot: 60% click-through to recos, 40% more time on site.
seo.resume_citable: As early as 2015, The North Face tested XPS, a conversational shopping assistant on IBM Watson that recommended products by use case and weather; the pilot reached 60% click-through to recommendations and 40% more time on site.

faq.q: Is The North Face's XPS assistant still in service?
faq.a: No, it no longer appears in production. Fluid's XPS unit was acquired by IBM in late 2016. It is a founding case of conversational advice, now carried forward by LLMs.

faq.q: What did it personalize the recommendation on?
faq.a: On the request expressed in natural language (activity, place, season), crossed with estimates of conditions such as temperature and wind.

pattern: Conversational shopping assistant that personalizes the product recommendation through dialogue (use case, weather, activity)
objectif_business: Reproduce online the advice of a specialist salesperson: ask a few questions about the intended use and surface the right products, rather than leaving the customer to filter a catalog alone.
description: In 2015-2016, The North Face put XPS (Expert Personal Shopper) online, a conversational shopping assistant built by the agency Fluid and powered by IBM Watson. The customer describes what they are looking for in natural language, for example a jacket for a hike at a given place and season; the system interprets the request, estimates the conditions (temperature, wind), and ranks the products accordingly. Launched in beta in December 2015 after a one-month pilot, the tool was at first limited to jackets. On the pilot, the average session lasted two minutes and the click-through rate to recommendations reached 60%. According to later accounts, customers who used the assistant spent 40% more time on the site and 75% said they would use it again. In November 2016, IBM acquired Fluid's XPS unit. The original setup no longer appears in service today; the pattern itself has become widespread with LLM-based conversational assistants.

resultats.metrique: Time on site with the assistant

niveau_preuve.justification: Official launch release (pilot figures: 60% click-through, 2-minute sessions) and consistent third-party analyst accounts for time on site and intent to reuse. No financial result; an old setup whose liveness is no longer confirmed.

stack_technique.detail: Cognitive technology (NLP) that interpreted the request in natural language and estimated the context (temperature, wind) for the place and season.
Conversational shopping assistant designed by the agency Fluid on Watson; the XPS unit was acquired by IBM in November 2016.
Integration point for the assistant, at first limited to the jackets category.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Real time, on the customer's request during their shopping session.
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: The brand's e-commerce / digital team, with the assistant provided by a technology partner (here Fluid on IBM Watson).
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The request expressed by the customer in natural language, crossed with context data (place, season, weather). Without a reliable mapping between intent and product attributes, the assistant recommends off target.

etapes.detail: The customer states their need in natural language (activity, place, season).
NLP extracts the intent and estimates the conditions (temperature, wind) for the place and period.
Items are ordered by fit to the stated need and context, then presented to the customer.
Time on site, clicks to recommendations, and intent to reuse serve to judge the tool.

prerequis_data: A catalog with usable use-case attributes (activity, season, conditions)
A mapping between customer intents and product attributes
An external context source if relevant (weather, location)
prerequis_orga: An e-commerce team to maintain the intent-to-product mapping
stack_possible: An LLM-based conversational assistant (Azure OpenAI, Google, or equivalent) connected to the catalog
A contextual recommendation engine behind the assistant
replication.premiere_etape: Target a category with a high need for advice (outdoor gear, tech), connect a conversational assistant to the catalog, and measure click-through to recos and conversion against the classic filtered path.

playbook.action: Pick a category with a high need for advice and map the catalog's use-case attributes (activity, season, conditions).
playbook.livrable: Mapping of customer intent to product attributes.

playbook.action: Connect a conversational assistant (on an LLM today) to the category catalog, with guardrails and transparency about its AI nature.
playbook.livrable: Assistant in pre-production on the pilot category.

playbook.action: Open in beta on part of the traffic and measure click-through to recommendations, time on site, and conversion against the classic filtered path.
Iterate on the intent-to-product mapping from real conversations and decide on extending to other categories.

replication.equipe: 1 e-commerce PM + 1-2 devs + 1 catalog owner to maintain the intent-to-product mapping.

statut_vivant.note: The original XPS setup (Watson plus Fluid) appears to have been withdrawn long ago; Fluid's XPS unit was acquired by IBM in late 2016. The pattern (conversational shopping assistant) is by contrast very much alive, now carried by LLMs. Read this case as a founding one, not a feature in production.

transposable_ue.note: A conversational shopping assistant on an e-commerce site, transposable to the EU. A 2025 equivalent would rely on LLMs and fall under the AI Act's transparency obligations for generative AI. Note: the original setup (Watson XPS) is old and no longer appears in service.
